selection.early_exit_advice: No positions, so there is nothing to exit. Recorded only: re-evaluate at next week's rebalance using sources with verifiable timestamps.
selection.reason: Cash decision: no picks. I looked at post-earnings candidates (LLY after its Q3 beat and raise, MA and V after their beats), but my search tool could confirm only calendar dates for those reports, not a publication time with a timezone. The protocol rejects bare dates and forbids inventing times, so that evidence is omitted and cannot support a pick. The one source with a usable time covers the market backdrop only: a rebound with falling oil, which gives no stock-specific edge. Scheduled event risk from earnings and the midterm elections was also seen in sources that could not be time-verified, so it is not relied on here. This is an evidence-quality abstention, not a bearish market call; 100% cash is likely to lag SPY if the rebound continues.

sources.claim: Yahoo Finance's Nov. 2 live coverage reported US stocks recovering from a sell-off as oil prices fell, with the Dow up about 1.1% and the S&P 500 up about 1%. The 10:47 a.m. time is the page's update time as relayed by the search tool; the -05:00 offset is inferred from the EST label on the page's quote. A follow-up search could not reconfirm the update time.

selection.early_exit_advice: No positions to exit. Keep the weekly rebalance schedule; advice is recorded only.
selection.reason: Retain all $10,000 in cash for this weekly shadow interval. No sufficiently supported one-week excess-return thesis emerged from the verified evidence. Amazon's accelerating cloud growth is offset by negative free cash flow and cautious holiday guidance; the packet already shows a roughly 4.7% advance from its previous close. Strong semiconductor momentum alone does not establish a fresh catalyst. This is an abstention under uncertainty, not a confident prediction that cash will beat SPY.

sources.claim: Amazon reported below-consensus third-quarter results and a cautious fourth-quarter sales outlook, despite AWS growth of 39.3%.
The page identifies EDGAR availability at 4:06 PM EDT and reproduces Amazon's earnings filing: trailing-year free cash outflow was $42.4 billion, while AWS quarterly sales reached $46 billion.
